entry.title: SRF accepted wakes to 0.10 $B overnight: 67.5 sigma on a near-zero base, not a large flow
entry.summary: The board reads 45 out of 100, EROSION; the dated reserve path contributes 11.0 points; the pooled five-business-day event read is 6.4%; plumbing leads market pricing by +32 percentile points. The index is -0.3 against the last published letter.
entry.content:
Issue 47 · 2026-08-27 · the sections run in the same order every day, so the delta takes a minute to extract.

The argument

The calendar is carrying the strain call; the price of overnight cash still says abundance.

The board reads 45 out of 100, EROSION; the dated reserve path contributes 11.0 points; the pooled five-business-day event read is 6.4%; plumbing leads market pricing by +32 percentile points.

  • Balance-sheet identity, as of 2026-08-26: Reserves fell $10.4B on the week to $2,925B, and the ledger says where from: the foreign RRP pool released $17.9B, the residual absorbed $14.9B, the balance sheet shrank $14.8B, six legs summing to the reserve change to the dollar with $22.9B of the balance sheet, 0.34% of assets, still sitting in the unnamed residual. Source: Federal Reserve H.4.1.
  • Official-sector footprint, as of 2026-08-26: Foreign officials cut their Fed custody Treasuries by $64.4B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose by $56.4B, a parking rotation rather than the official bid leaving, footprint $2,971B. Source: Federal Reserve custody and foreign RRP.
  • Reserve-demand curve, as of 2026-08-26: Reserves are $779B below the fitted kink, but SOFR is -0.9bp versus IORB; fit R-squared is 0.62. Source: FRED, NY Fed secured rates, BEA GDP.

The countercase: SOFR is 0.9bp below IORB, a current abundance signal rather than a scarcity print. Standing Repo Facility take-up is $0.10B; the backstop is not being tested in size.

Conviction: GUARDED. The read is led by modelled or slow-moving structure while current market plumbing has not broadly confirmed it.

1 · The reading

The composite reads 45 out of 100, EROSION, -0.3 against the last published reading, on 100% coverage. Nothing is breaking. The margin for error is what is shrinking.

The heaviest hand on the dial is the calendar squeeze (weather) at a score of 100, worth +11.0 points of the total. Pinned at the ceiling today: the calendar squeeze (weather), the cash buffers, RRP and TGA (buffers). Those components are carrying no new information from day to day, and the letter names every one of them rather than only the loudest. When one component carries the reading, watch that component, not the headline.

Change gets attributed here, not just level: against the last letter, the tail law (tails) -0.1, reserve scarcity (kink) -0.1, the swap-line confession (confession) -0.1, auction digestion (auctions) +0.1, -0.2 points net across the components.

2 · What moved

Overnight, the tape did move: SRF accepted printed 0.10 $B (level z +67.5, change z +16.5, as of 2026-08-27); 2y Treasury constant maturity yield printed 4.19 % (level z +2.5, change z +0.5, as of 2026-08-26).

One qualification on that list: the 2y Treasury constant maturity yield flag is on LEVEL, not on change. The series sits somewhere unusual in its own history and did not travel to get there today, which is worth knowing and is not the same claim as a move.

For scale: that SRF accepted print is 0.10 $B against a historical peak near 75 $B. The z score marks a series waking up on a quiet baseline, not a large flow; the dollar amount is de minimis and the letter says so next to the sigma.

Still flagged from prints already covered in an earlier letter: Sri Lankan rupees per USD (H.10) (|z| 2.8, as of 2026-08-21). A standing flag is context, not news; when a fresh print lands it goes back in the movers line.

Repo held under the SRF ceiling for all of the last 20 sessions with SRF take-up at $0.1B, stigma score 0 of 100, the backstop is capping quietly.

3 · The Tell

The Tell, the gap between what the pipes measure and what the screens price, reads +31.7: plumbing indicators at the 58.0 percentile of their own history, market indicators at the 26.0, a gap of +32.0.

A gap this wide has a short shelf life. The board's read is plumbing leads price, and the record of what happened after past gaps sits in PROOF.

4 · Reserve scarcity

The desk fits the reserve demand curve continuously, a public-data approximation of the NY Fed's monthly Reserve Demand Elasticity (the Afonso, Giannone, La Spada and Williams lineage). Theirs is estimated on confidential bank-level fed funds transactions; this one is a hinge fit on SOFR minus IORB against reserves over GDP, which is a different and coarser instrument reaching for the same quantity, and the comparison below is the check on whether it gets there. Today's fit puts the kink near $3,704B of reserves; the system holds $2,925B, $779B below the estimate.

Fit honesty: R² 0.62 against a flat curve; the observed SOFR minus IORB spread of -0.9bp versus the fit's -0.2bp gives a consistency of 0.94. A modest fit is a lens, not a verdict, and the number is printed so you can discount it yourself.

Reserves are through the estimated kink, which is exactly where the spread should start answering to reserve changes. From here the board watches the slope, not the distance. Against that, the tape disagrees: SOFR is printing 0.9bp BELOW IORB, which is the abundance signature, not the scarce one. The honest reading is that the fitted kink is an estimate with a wide band and the observed spread is a fact, so scarcity here is a hypothesis the tape has not yet confirmed.

Reserves fell $10.4B on the week to $2,925B, and the ledger says where from: the foreign RRP pool released $17.9B, the residual absorbed $14.9B, the balance sheet shrank $14.8B, six legs summing to the reserve change to the dollar with $22.9B of the balance sheet, 0.34% of assets, still sitting in the unnamed residual.

External check: the NY Fed's latest official RDE print (2026-08-13) reads -0.37bp per one percent of reserves; the desk's continuous fit implies -0.29bp, inside their 68% band, direction agrees. The desk's fit runs 13 days ahead of their release cycle, which is the whole point of fitting it continuously. Where the two diverge, one of us is wrong, and the scorecard keeps count.

The running record, not just today: across 18 of their releases the desk's walk-forward fit landed inside their 68% band 9 times and agreed on direction 10 times, mean absolute gap 0.25bp. That is short of the two-in-three a calibrated nowcast should manage, so the fit is directionally useful and not yet precise. One matching print is an anecdote; this line is the claim, and it is graded against their current-vintage history rather than the print that stood on each cutoff date, which flatters neither side in a way the desk can measure.

5 · The official sector

Foreign officials cut their Fed custody Treasuries by $64.4B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose by $56.4B, a parking rotation rather than the official bid leaving, footprint $2,971B.

6 · The dates that matter

The next date that matters is 2026-08-31: calendar pressure date while reserves sit below the estimated kink, worst case reserves near $2,882B after the drain. The turn model puts 2026-08-31 (month_end) at +3.5bp with a band of [-0.5, +8.2], severity 2/5. FOMC decides 2026-09-16, 20 days out. The corporate tax date lands 2026-09-15, 19 days out; tax dates drain reserves on a schedule everyone can read.

7 · What the board is honest about

All sources and engines report live. The misses this board has made sit in PROOF next to the hits; read those before weighting today's letter.

The desk's forward read

The court

Bathymetry puts the odds of an event inside five business days at 5%, mean first-passage roughly 77 business days. The learned model reads 7% for the same window and calls it does not out-rank the rule-based index. The regime chain gives 0% odds of touching STRESS inside 21 business days, with an expected dwell of 63 business days in the current state. Resonance reads 66: the Year-end (G-SIB surcharge snapshot) mode is amplifying at 6.3x, which is the basin ringing louder to the same calendar.

The stack pools the members at 6% for the five-day window, dispersion 0.02, pooled over its own 6 members rather than the views quoted above. Its own verdict, in full: published signal = mean (Brier 0.0401 vs mean 0.0401, climatology 0.0391); does NOT beat the best single member (swell), the ensemble adds robustness, not skill.

Model Court, 5bd event odds: 4 models span 5.3 to 16.0 pct, pooled 10.8 pct (skill weighted, 2 of 4 beat climatology); live ranking withheld (24 of 30 resolved at worst).

Ledger status: ledger accruing: bathymetry 24/30 resolved (6 pending), ml 24/30 resolved (6 pending), stacker 24/30 resolved (6 pending), swell 24/30 resolved (6 pending), tidetables 24/30 resolved (6 pending); ranked verdict withheld until 30 resolved rows per model..

The supply desk

settlesbills $Bcoupons $Bmaturing $Bnet new cash $Bstatus
2026-08-272780271+7announced
2026-08-280280+28announced
2026-08-310234179+54announced
2026-09-012840275+9announced
2026-09-0330853326+35projected
2026-09-082840286-1projected
2026-09-102560278-22projected
2026-09-152840340-56projected

The heaviest settlement ahead is 2026-09-16 at $+73B net. Net new cash is the number that drains reserves. Maturing includes SOMA rollovers, so the private-side drain runs smaller on SOMA-heavy dates; projected rows are the desk's house estimate and get graded when Treasury announces.

The last auction on the board is the 7y note of 2026-08-27, graded C on a composite z of -0.14, and its funding window is still open at 0 of 4 marks, so the board is not scoring the plumbing yet, and the trailing indirect share for that tenor is softening.

Positioning

Leveraged funds hold $1,037B gross short in Treasury futures, $810B net short of it after longs. That is 78% of the gross standing one way, the signature of the cash-futures basis trade rather than a two-sided book. Neither number is a directional view by itself: the long cash leg that would offset a basis position is not in this dataset, and the letter will not price a bet it cannot see. The most crowded seat is UST 2Y NOTE at the 100th percentile of its own history, leveraged net -0.28 of open interest (z +2.7). The emptiest is SOFR-3M at the 6th, which is worth naming because an unusually light seat is a different risk from a heavy one and the ranking statistic alone does not distinguish them. Dealer warehouse holds $408B, the 95th percentile of its history, 36% of it long end, as of 2026-08-19. Futures positioning is CFTC Commitments of Traders and carries its native T+3 lag; the dealer warehouse is the NY Fed primary dealer survey, published with a longer lag again. The futures rows carry no as-of date on the board today, which is itself a gap and is reported rather than papered over. Every figure here is weeks old by construction and is a stock, not this morning's flow.

Echoes

episodewindowsimilarity
Mar 2020 dash-for-cashT−13d0.69
Sep 2025 tax-date squeeze (SOFR +18bp over EFFR)T−2d0.61
Apr 2025 tariff shock basis unwindT−30d0.60
Sep 2019 repo spike (SOFR 5.25%, GC 10%)T−3d0.58

The top rhyme is Mar 2020 dash-for-cash at 0.69, above the desk's 0.60 attention line. That line is an editorial convention, not a validated threshold: the engine publishes no null distribution for this distance, so nothing here says how often a 0.60 rhyme is a coincidence. Similarity is not destiny, and PROOF's outcome tables, not this one, carry what actually followed.

The ledger: what would change the desk's mind

  • E1 · The Tell closing back under +15; today it reads +32.
  • E2 · Reserves stabilising for two straight weeks; the current drain runs $-1.5B a business day.
  • E3 · Calendar amplification easing below 1x; today it runs 6.3x.

Resolution: the last letter's ledger was written for STRAIN; the regime moved to EROSION, so the items above are rewritten for the new state. The move itself is on the record in the composite history.

The board recomputes six times a day; this letter freezes one reading of it. Free public data with native lags. Not investment advice.

W4-3srf2026-08-31hit if next week's board shows a twenty session maximum take-up under the threshold, miss if any session prints at or above it
W4-4reserves2026-08-31hit if next week's board carries current reserves within tolerance of the target, miss otherwise

Reserve path assumptions, published beside the path

Start 2,935B on 2026-08-19, trailing drift -14.9B a week over 13 weeks, runoff $0B a month, TGA $936B now against a median of $860B and a p75 of $926B, ON RRP $0.2B, settlements $477B gross counted at 25% passthrough.

  • arithmetic on stated assumptions, not a forecast of policy
  • the trailing drift already embeds recent QT, settlement and fiscal flows, so the settlement term enters as a deviation from the calendar's own weekly mean (shape, not level) and only the explicit QT pace can still double count against the drift
  • settlement drains counted at 25% of gross (rollover assumption) before demeaning

What the supply table does not know

  • rows marked issuance_incomplete sit past the announced horizon on a date whose maturities are known but whose refunding issuance is not projected (quarterly originals have no short cadence to extrapolate); their net is an artifact, not a forecast, and should not be read as a drain
  • maturing includes Fed SOMA holdings, which roll over at auction; net new cash to private investors is smaller on SOMA-heavy dates
  • Treasury buyback retirements are not netted from the maturing stock
  • TBA offering amounts are filled with the tenor's last realized size (amount_estimated=true)
  • projected rows carry each tenor's last size forward at its observed cadence; tenors without a regular cadence under 5 weeks (quarterly refunding originals, one-off CMBs) are not projected

The calls above were written before the week ran and are stored in the letter's own state file, so next Monday's issue grades exactly this list and not a convenient subset of it. entry.content:
Issue 43 · 2026-08-23 · the sections run in the same order every day, so the delta takes a minute to extract.

The argument

The calendar is carrying the strain call; the price of overnight cash still says abundance.

The board reads 45 out of 100, STRAIN; the dated reserve path contributes 11.0 points; the pooled five-business-day event read is 5.9%; plumbing leads market pricing by +23 percentile points.

  • Balance-sheet identity, as of 2026-08-19: Reserves fell $8.8B on the week to $2,935B, and the ledger says where from: the foreign RRP pool absorbed $16.0B, the balance sheet shrank $14.3B, the residual released $10.9B, six legs summing to the reserve change to the dollar with $8.0B of the balance sheet, 0.12% of assets, still sitting in the unnamed residual. Source: Federal Reserve H.4.1.
  • Official-sector footprint, as of 2026-08-19: Foreign officials cut their Fed custody Treasuries by $80.7B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose by $55.6B, only a partial rotation because the combined official footprint still fell $25.0B to $2,960B, 31% of the custody drop leaving the official sector rather than moving inside it. Source: Federal Reserve custody and foreign RRP.
  • Reserve-demand curve, as of 2026-08-19: Reserves are $768B below the fitted kink, but SOFR is -0.9bp versus IORB; fit R-squared is 0.62. Source: FRED, NY Fed secured rates, BEA GDP.

The countercase: SOFR is 0.9bp below IORB, a current abundance signal rather than a scarcity print. Standing Repo Facility take-up is $0.00B; the backstop is not being tested in size.

Conviction: GUARDED. The read is led by modelled or slow-moving structure while current market plumbing has not broadly confirmed it.

1 · The reading

The composite reads 45 out of 100, STRAIN, +0.0 against the last published reading, on 100% coverage. The pipes are working harder for the same result. This is the regime where surprises stop being cheap.

The heaviest hand on the dial is the calendar squeeze (weather) at a score of 100, worth +11.0 points of the total. Pinned at the ceiling today: the calendar squeeze (weather), the cash buffers, RRP and TGA (buffers). Those components are carrying no new information from day to day, and the letter names every one of them rather than only the loudest. When one component carries the reading, watch that component, not the headline.

Component by component, the reading is flat against the last letter: no contribution moved a tenth of a point. Flat gets said too.

2 · What moved

Nothing new crossed the ±2.5 robust z bar overnight. The standing flags below are persistence, not news, and the letter labels them as such.

Still flagged from prints already covered in an earlier letter: 2y Treasury constant maturity yield (|z| 2.6, as of 2026-08-20). A standing flag is context, not news; when a fresh print lands it goes back in the movers line.

The tape is quiet, so the forward odds do the talking. Bathymetry puts the odds of an event inside five business days at 4%, mean first-passage roughly 77 business days. The learned model reads 2% for the same window and calls it does not out-rank the rule-based index. The regime chain gives 0% odds of touching STRESS inside 21 business days, with an expected dwell of 11 business days in the current state.

Repo held under the SRF ceiling for all of the last 20 sessions with SRF take-up at $0.0B, stigma score 0 of 100, the backstop is capping quietly.

3 · The Tell

The Tell, the gap between what the pipes measure and what the screens price, reads +23.3: plumbing indicators at the 58.0 percentile of their own history, market indicators at the 35.0, a gap of +23.0.

The gap is modest. Modest gaps are what most days look like, and saying so is part of the record.

4 · Reserve scarcity

The desk fits the reserve demand curve continuously, a public-data approximation of the NY Fed's monthly Reserve Demand Elasticity (the Afonso, Giannone, La Spada and Williams lineage). Theirs is estimated on confidential bank-level fed funds transactions; this one is a hinge fit on SOFR minus IORB against reserves over GDP, which is a different and coarser instrument reaching for the same quantity, and the comparison below is the check on whether it gets there. Today's fit puts the kink near $3,703B of reserves; the system holds $2,935B, $768B below the estimate.

Fit honesty: R² 0.62 against a flat curve; the observed SOFR minus IORB spread of -0.9bp versus the fit's -0.3bp gives a consistency of 0.95. A modest fit is a lens, not a verdict, and the number is printed so you can discount it yourself.

Reserves are through the estimated kink, which is exactly where the spread should start answering to reserve changes. From here the board watches the slope, not the distance. Against that, the tape disagrees: SOFR is printing 0.9bp BELOW IORB, which is the abundance signature, not the scarce one. The honest reading is that the fitted kink is an estimate with a wide band and the observed spread is a fact, so scarcity here is a hypothesis the tape has not yet confirmed.

Reserves fell $8.8B on the week to $2,935B, and the ledger says where from: the foreign RRP pool absorbed $16.0B, the balance sheet shrank $14.3B, the residual released $10.9B, six legs summing to the reserve change to the dollar with $8.0B of the balance sheet, 0.12% of assets, still sitting in the unnamed residual.

External check: the NY Fed's latest official RDE print (2026-08-13) reads -0.37bp per one percent of reserves; the desk's continuous fit implies -0.29bp, inside their 68% band, direction agrees. The desk's fit runs 6 days ahead of their release cycle, which is the whole point of fitting it continuously. Where the two diverge, one of us is wrong, and the scorecard keeps count.

The running record, not just today: across 18 of their releases the desk's walk-forward fit landed inside their 68% band 9 times and agreed on direction 10 times, mean absolute gap 0.25bp. That is short of the two-in-three a calibrated nowcast should manage, so the fit is directionally useful and not yet precise. One matching print is an anecdote; this line is the claim, and it is graded against their current-vintage history rather than the print that stood on each cutoff date, which flatters neither side in a way the desk can measure.

5 · The official sector

Foreign officials cut their Fed custody Treasuries by $80.7B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose by $55.6B, only a partial rotation because the combined official footprint still fell $25.0B to $2,960B, 31% of the custody drop leaving the official sector rather than moving inside it.

6 · The dates that matter

The next date that matters is 2026-08-27: $266B auction settlement while reserves sit below the estimated kink, worst case reserves near $2,895B after the drain. The turn model puts 2026-08-31 (month_end) at +2.2bp with a band of [-1.8, +6.9], severity 1/5. FOMC decides 2026-09-16, 24 days out. The corporate tax date lands 2026-09-15, 23 days out; tax dates drain reserves on a schedule everyone can read.

7 · What the board is honest about

All sources and engines report live. The misses this board has made sit in PROOF next to the hits; read those before weighting today's letter.

The desk's forward read

The court

Bathymetry puts the odds of an event inside five business days at 4%, mean first-passage roughly 77 business days. The learned model reads 2% for the same window and calls it does not out-rank the rule-based index. The regime chain gives 0% odds of touching STRESS inside 21 business days, with an expected dwell of 11 business days in the current state. The last auction on the board is the 4w bill of 2026-08-20, graded C on a composite z of -0.29, and its funding window is still open at 1 of 4 marks, so the board is not scoring the plumbing yet.

Positioning

Leveraged funds hold $1,037B gross short in Treasury futures, $810B net short of it after longs. That is 78% of the gross standing one way, the signature of the cash-futures basis trade rather than a two-sided book. The futures rows carry no as-of date on the board today, which is itself a gap and is reported rather than papered over. Every figure here is weeks old by construction and is a stock, not this morning's flow.

Similarity is not destiny, and PROOF's outcome tables, not this one, carry what actually followed.

The ledger: what would change the desk's mind

  • S1 · SRF or discount window take-up above $1B on a day with no calendar excuse; discount window $5.0B as of 2026-08-19. That is through the $1B line already, so this item reads BREACHED and the standing read is that discount window borrowing is elevated against its own recent history, not that nothing has happened.
  • S2 · A funding-side mover breaching ±3 robust z on a fresh print.
  • S3 · The composite crossing 60; today it reads 45.

When one of those prints, the letter will say so, in this same place, with the number. The IDs are stable, so hold the desk to them.

3 · The Tell

The Tell, the gap between what the pipes measure and what the screens price, reads +38.7: plumbing indicators at the 63.0 percentile of their own history, market indicators at the 24.0, a gap of +39.0.

entry.content:
Issue 36 · 2026-08-16 · the sections run in the same order every day, so the delta takes a minute to extract.

The argument

The calendar is carrying the strain call; the price of overnight cash still says abundance.

The board reads 45 out of 100, STRAIN; the dated reserve path contributes 11.0 points; the pooled five-business-day event read is 6.6%; plumbing leads market pricing by +37 percentile points.

  • Balance-sheet identity, as of 2026-08-12: Reserves fell $49.3B on the week to $2,944B, and the ledger says where from: the TGA rebuilt $56.6B, the foreign RRP pool absorbed $39.7B, the residual released $36.5B, six legs summing to the reserve change to the dollar with $18.9B of the balance sheet, 0.28% of assets, still sitting in the unnamed residual. Source: Federal Reserve H.4.1.
  • Official-sector footprint, as of 2026-08-12: Foreign officials cut their Fed custody Treasuries by $90.2B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose by $34.8B, only a partial rotation because the combined official footprint still fell $55.5B to $2,954B, 62% of the custody drop leaving the official sector rather than moving inside it. Source: Federal Reserve custody and foreign RRP.
  • Reserve-demand curve, as of 2026-08-12: Reserves are $759B below the fitted kink, but SOFR is -1.7bp versus IORB; fit R-squared is 0.62. Source: FRED, NY Fed secured rates, BEA GDP.

The countercase: SOFR is 1.7bp below IORB, a current abundance signal rather than a scarcity print. Standing Repo Facility take-up is $0.00B; the backstop is not being tested in size.

Conviction: LOW. A source or engine fault reduces the evidence set; confidence is cut before the index is interpreted.

1 · The reading

The composite reads 45 out of 100, STRAIN, +0.0 against the last published reading, on 100% coverage. The pipes are working harder for the same result. This is the regime where surprises stop being cheap.

The heaviest hand on the dial is the calendar squeeze (weather) at a score of 100, worth +11.0 points of the total. Pinned at the ceiling today: the calendar squeeze (weather), the cash buffers, RRP and TGA (buffers). Those components are carrying no new information from day to day, and the letter names every one of them rather than only the loudest. When one component carries the reading, watch that component, not the headline.

Component by component, the reading is flat against the last letter: no contribution moved a tenth of a point. Flat gets said too.

2 · What moved

No new print cleared the ±2.5 robust z bar since the last letter. What is flagged today was flagged when it printed, and re-breaking old news is not this letter's trade.

Still flagged from prints already covered in an earlier letter: Reverse repo with foreign official accounts (|z| 3.8, as of 2026-08-12); Canadian dollars per USD (H.10) (|z| 2.8, as of 2026-08-07); S&P 500 index (|z| 2.5, as of 2026-08-14). A standing flag is context, not news; when a fresh print lands it goes back in the movers line.

With nothing new on the tape, the forward read carries the letter. Bathymetry puts the odds of an event inside five business days at 5%, mean first-passage roughly 77 business days. The learned model reads 3% for the same window and calls it does not out-rank the rule-based index. The regime chain gives 0% odds of touching STRESS inside 21 business days, with an expected dwell of 11 business days in the current state.

Repo held under the SRF ceiling for all of the last 20 sessions with SRF take-up at $0.0B, stigma score 0 of 100, the backstop is capping quietly.

3 · The Tell

The Tell, the gap between what the pipes measure and what the screens price, reads +37.1: plumbing indicators at the 64.0 percentile of their own history, market indicators at the 27.0, a gap of +37.0.

A gap this wide has a short shelf life. The board's read is plumbing leads price, and the record of what happened after past gaps sits in PROOF.

4 · Reserve scarcity

The desk fits the reserve demand curve continuously, a public-data approximation of the NY Fed's monthly Reserve Demand Elasticity (the Afonso, Giannone, La Spada and Williams lineage). Theirs is estimated on confidential bank-level fed funds transactions; this one is a hinge fit on SOFR minus IORB against reserves over GDP, which is a different and coarser instrument reaching for the same quantity, and the comparison below is the check on whether it gets there. Today's fit puts the kink near $3,703B of reserves; the system holds $2,944B, $759B below the estimate.

Fit honesty: R² 0.62 against a flat curve; the observed SOFR minus IORB spread of -1.7bp versus the fit's -0.4bp gives a consistency of 0.89. A modest fit is a lens, not a verdict, and the number is printed so you can discount it yourself.

Reserves are through the estimated kink, which is exactly where the spread should start answering to reserve changes. From here the board watches the slope, not the distance. Against that, the tape disagrees: SOFR is printing 1.7bp BELOW IORB, which is the abundance signature, not the scarce one. The honest reading is that the fitted kink is an estimate with a wide band and the observed spread is a fact, so scarcity here is a hypothesis the tape has not yet confirmed.

Reserves fell $49.3B on the week to $2,944B, and the ledger says where from: the TGA rebuilt $56.6B, the foreign RRP pool absorbed $39.7B, the residual released $36.5B, six legs summing to the reserve change to the dollar with $18.9B of the balance sheet, 0.28% of assets, still sitting in the unnamed residual.

External check: the NY Fed's latest official RDE print (2026-07-06) reads -0.27bp per one percent of reserves; the desk's continuous fit implies -0.30bp, inside their 68% band, direction agrees. The desk's fit runs 37 days ahead of their release cycle, which is the whole point of fitting it continuously. Where the two diverge, one of us is wrong, and the scorecard keeps count.

The running record, not just today: across 18 of their releases the desk's walk-forward fit landed inside their 68% band 8 times and agreed on direction 10 times, mean absolute gap 0.26bp. That is short of the two-in-three a calibrated nowcast should manage, so the fit is directionally useful and not yet precise. One matching print is an anecdote; this line is the claim, and it is graded against their current-vintage history rather than the print that stood on each cutoff date, which flatters neither side in a way the desk can measure.

5 · The official sector

Foreign officials cut their Fed custody Treasuries by $90.2B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose by $34.8B, only a partial rotation because the combined official footprint still fell $55.5B to $2,954B, 62% of the custody drop leaving the official sector rather than moving inside it.

6 · The dates that matter

The next date that matters is 2026-08-20: $266B auction settlement while reserves sit below the estimated kink, worst case reserves near $2,882B after the drain. The turn model puts 2026-08-31 (month_end) at +2.2bp with a band of [-1.7, +6.7], severity 1/5. FOMC decides 2026-09-16, 31 days out. The corporate tax date lands 2026-09-15, 30 days out; tax dates drain reserves on a schedule everyone can read.

7 · What the board is honest about

Faults on the board today: bis. The affected inputs are degraded or dead and the composite's coverage says so. A dashboard that hides its broken gauges is lying with a straight face. The misses this board has made sit in PROOF next to the hits; read those before weighting today's letter.

The desk's forward read

The court

Bathymetry puts the odds of an event inside five business days at 5%, mean first-passage roughly 77 business days. The learned model reads 3% for the same window and calls it does not out-rank the rule-based index. The regime chain gives 0% odds of touching STRESS inside 21 business days, with an expected dwell of 11 business days in the current state. Resonance reads 66: the Year-end (G-SIB surcharge snapshot) mode is amplifying at 6.3x, which is the basin ringing louder to the same calendar.

The stack pools the members at 7% for the five-day window, dispersion 0.02, pooled over its own 6 members rather than the views quoted above. Its own verdict, in full: published signal = mean (Brier 0.0404 vs mean 0.0404, climatology 0.0393); does NOT beat the best single member (swell), the ensemble adds robustness, not skill.

Model Court, 5bd event odds: 4 models span 3.1 to 12.0 pct, pooled 9.5 pct (skill weighted, 1 of 4 beat climatology); live ranking withheld (13 of 30 resolved at worst).

The supply desk

The last auction on the board is the 30y bond of 2026-08-13, graded B on a composite z of -0.47, and its funding window is still open at 1 of 4 marks, so the board is not scoring the plumbing yet.

Positioning

Leveraged funds hold $1,048B gross short in Treasury futures, $825B net short of it after longs. That is 79% of the gross standing one way, the signature of the cash-futures basis trade rather than a two-sided book. Neither number is a directional view by itself: the long cash leg that would offset a basis position is not in this dataset, and the letter will not price a bet it cannot see. The most crowded seat is UST 2Y NOTE at the 99th percentile of its own history, leveraged net -0.31 of open interest (z +2.2). The emptiest is SOFR-3M at the 4th, which is worth naming because an unusually light seat is a different risk from a heavy one and the ranking statistic alone does not distinguish them. Dealer warehouse holds $424B, the 96th percentile of its history, 35% of it long end, as of 2026-08-05. Futures positioning is CFTC Commitments of Traders and carries its native T+3 lag; the dealer warehouse is the NY Fed primary dealer survey, published with a longer lag again. The futures rows carry no as-of date on the board today, which is itself a gap and is reported rather than papered over. Every figure here is weeks old by construction and is a stock, not this morning's flow.

Echoes

The top rhyme is Mar 2020 dash-for-cash at 0.68, above the desk's 0.60 attention line. That line is an editorial convention, not a validated threshold: the engine publishes no null distribution for this distance, so nothing here says how often a 0.60 rhyme is a coincidence. Similarity is not destiny, and PROOF's outcome tables, not this one, carry what actually followed.

The ledger: what would change the desk's mind

  • S1 · SRF or discount window take-up above $1B on a day with no calendar excuse; discount window $5.6B as of 2026-08-12. That is through the $1B line already, so this item reads BREACHED and the standing read is that discount window borrowing is elevated against its own recent history, not that nothing has happened.
  • S2 · A funding-side mover breaching ±3 robust z on a fresh print.
  • S3 · The composite crossing 60; today it reads 45.

When one of those prints, the letter will say so, in this same place, with the number. The IDs are stable, so hold the desk to them.

entry.title: Strain with a loud tell: plumbing leads price at +32
entry.summary: The composite reads 46, regime STRAIN. That is +0.2 on the day. The Tell reads +32. Every number below is checkable on the board.
entry.content:
Issue 23 · 2026-08-03 · the sections run in the same order every day, so the delta takes a minute to extract.

1 · The reading

The composite reads 46 out of 100, STRAIN, +0.2 against the last published reading, on 100% coverage. The pipes are working harder for the same result. This is the regime where surprises stop being cheap.

The heaviest hand on the dial is the calendar squeeze (weather) at a score of 100, worth +11.0 points of the total. Pinned at the ceiling today: the calendar squeeze (weather), the cash buffers, RRP and TGA (buffers). Those components are carrying no new information from day to day, and the letter names every one of them rather than only the loudest. When one component carries the reading, watch that component, not the headline.

Change gets attributed here, not just level: against the last letter, the tail law (tails) +0.2, +0.2 points net across the components.

2 · What moved

Nothing new crossed the ±2.5 robust z bar overnight. The standing flags below are persistence, not news, and the letter labels them as such.

Still flagged from prints already covered in an earlier letter: Central bank liquidity swaps outstanding (H.4.1) (|z| 15.7, as of 2026-07-29) [de minimis]; CBOE VIX index (|z| 3.4, as of 2026-07-30); Discount window primary credit (Wed level) (|z| 3.4, as of 2026-07-29). A standing flag is context, not news; when a fresh print lands it goes back in the movers line. The flags marked de minimis (Central bank liquidity swaps outstanding (H.4.1)) sit at large sigma on series whose levels are a rounding error against their own history: the standardizer is reacting to a near-zero baseline, not to a large flow, and the letter would rather say that every day than let a big number do work the dollars do not support.

No fresh print does not mean no information; the odds recompute either way. Bathymetry puts the odds of an event inside five business days at 6%, mean first-passage roughly 75 business days. The learned model reads 8% for the same window and calls it does not out-rank the rule-based index. The regime chain gives 0% odds of touching STRESS inside 21 business days, with an expected dwell of 11 business days in the current state.

Repo held under the SRF ceiling for all of the last 20 sessions with SRF take-up at $0.0B, stigma score 0 of 100, the backstop is capping quietly.

3 · The Tell

The Tell, the gap between what the pipes measure and what the screens price, reads +32.1: plumbing indicators at the 68.0th percentile of their own history, market indicators at the 36.0th, a gap of +32.0.

That is a wide disagreement, and it resolves one of two ways: the screens catch up to the pipes, or the pipes calm down to meet the screens. The reading is plumbing leads price.

4 · Reserve scarcity

The desk fits the reserve demand curve continuously, a public-data approximation of the NY Fed's monthly Reserve Demand Elasticity (the Afonso, Giannone, La Spada and Williams lineage). Theirs is estimated on confidential bank-level fed funds transactions; this one is a hinge fit on SOFR minus IORB against reserves over GDP, which is a different and coarser instrument reaching for the same quantity, and the comparison below is the check on whether it gets there. Today's fit puts the kink near $3,704B of reserves; the system holds $2,985B, $719B below the estimate.

Fit honesty: R² 0.62 against a flat curve; the observed SOFR minus IORB spread of -3.7bp versus the fit's -0.8bp gives a consistency of 0.76. A modest fit is a lens, not a verdict, and the number is printed so you can discount it yourself.

Reserves are through the estimated kink, which is exactly where the spread should start answering to reserve changes. From here the board watches the slope, not the distance. Against that, the tape disagrees: SOFR is printing 3.7bp BELOW IORB, which is the abundance signature, not the scarce one. The honest reading is that the fitted kink is an estimate with a wide band and the observed spread is a fact, so scarcity here is a hypothesis the tape has not yet confirmed.

Reserves fell $77.6B on the week to $2,985B, and the ledger says where from: the TGA rebuilt $81.2B, the foreign RRP pool released $17.9B, the balance sheet shrank $9.2B, six legs summing to the reserve change to the dollar with $34.8B of the balance sheet, 0.52% of assets, still sitting in the unnamed residual.

External check: the NY Fed's latest official RDE print (2026-07-06) reads -0.27bp per one percent of reserves; the desk's continuous fit implies -0.30bp, inside their 68% band, direction agrees. The desk's fit runs 23 days ahead of their release cycle, which is the whole point of fitting it continuously. Where the two diverge, one of us is wrong, and the scorecard keeps count.

The running record, not just today: across 18 of their releases the desk's walk-forward fit landed inside their 68% band 8 times and agreed on direction 10 times, mean absolute gap 0.26bp. That is short of the two-in-three a calibrated nowcast should manage, so the fit is directionally useful and not yet precise. One matching print is an anecdote; this line is the claim, and it is graded against their current-vintage history rather than the print that stood on each cutoff date, which flatters neither side in a way the desk can measure.

5 · The official sector

Foreign officials cut their Fed custody Treasuries by $78.4B over 13 weeks while foreign RRP parking rose by $12.5B, only a partial rotation because the combined official footprint still fell $65.9B to $2,991B, 84% of the custody drop leaving the official sector rather than moving inside it.

6 · The dates that matter

The next date that matters is 2026-07-31: calendar pressure date while reserves sit below the estimated kink, worst case reserves near $2,966B after the drain. The turn model puts 2026-08-31 (month_end) at +4.2bp with a band of [+0.3, +8.3], severity 2/5. FOMC decides 2026-09-16, 44 days out. The corporate tax date lands 2026-09-15, 43 days out; tax dates drain reserves on a schedule everyone can read.

7 · What the board is honest about

Faults on the board today: gdelt. The affected inputs are degraded or dead and the composite's coverage says so. A dashboard that hides its broken gauges is lying with a straight face. The record is in PROOF: event recall 62% (95% interval 36% to 82%, which is wide because the sample is 23 alert runs, not thousands) against a base rate of 4%, run precision 17%, and the median lead of 60 trading days is censored: 7 of 8 episodes were still flagged at the edge of the evaluation window, so the true lead is at least that and the number is a floor rather than a central estimate. The misses sit next to the hits; read those before weighting today's letter.

The desk's forward read

The court

Bathymetry puts the odds of an event inside five business days at 6%, mean first-passage roughly 75 business days. The learned model reads 8% for the same window and calls it does not out-rank the rule-based index. The regime chain gives 0% odds of touching STRESS inside 21 business days, with an expected dwell of 11 business days in the current state. Resonance reads 71: the Year-end (G-SIB surcharge snapshot) mode is amplifying at 6.3x, which is the basin ringing louder to the same calendar.

The stack pools the members at 8% for the five-day window, dispersion 0.01, pooled over its own 6 members rather than the views quoted above. Its own verdict, in full: published signal = mean (Brier 0.0405 vs mean 0.0405, climatology 0.0395); does NOT beat the best single member (swell), the ensemble adds robustness, not skill.

Model Court, 5bd event odds: 4 models span 6.4 to 12.0 pct, pooled 8.2 pct (skill weighted, 2 of 4 beat climatology); live ranking withheld (0 of 30 resolved at worst).

Reserve path assumptions, published beside the path

  • arithmetic on stated assumptions, not a forecast of policy

  • maturing includes Fed SOMA holdings, which roll over at auction; net new cash to private investors is smaller on SOMA-heavy dates

3 · The Tell

The Tell, the gap between what the pipes measure and what the screens price, reads +12.6: plumbing indicators at the 53.0th percentile of their own history, market indicators at the 41.0th, a gap of +12.0.

The gap is modest. Modest gaps are what most days look like, and saying so is part of the record.

4 · Reserve scarcity

The desk fits the reserve demand curve continuously, a public-data approximation of the NY Fed's monthly Reserve Demand Elasticity (the Afonso, Giannone, La Spada and Williams lineage).
